defects.description: Execution authorizes a deferred edit with its old membership snapshot instead of current project membership.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import { Workspace } from "./src/workspace.js"; const w=new Workspace(); w.createProject("p","alice"); w.policy.grant("p","alice","bob","editor"); w.createDocument("alice","d","p","Draft"); const j=w.prepare("bob","d",{title:"Published"}); w.policy.revoke("p","alice","bob"); try {w.apply(j)} catch {} console.log(w.read("alice","d").title);'

defects.why_missed: S9(a): prepare, revoke, apply crosses a membership change. Policy snapshots are correct historical views and Store updates are correct unauthenticated persistence; Workspace composes them as live authority.

defects.description: Renewing a permanently revoked recipient token restores access.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import { Workspace } from "./src/workspace.js"; import { Links } from "./src/links.js"; const w=new Workspace(); w.createProject("p","alice"); w.createDocument("alice","d","p","Draft"); const l=new Links(w,()=>10); const k=l.issue("alice","d","guest",20); l.revoke("alice",k); l.renew("alice",k,30); let out="denied"; try {out=l.read("guest",k).title} catch {} console.log(out);'

defects.why_missed: S9(a,d): issue, revoke, renew, read. Naive renewal tests expect usable links, whereas the secondary contract makes revocation permanent.
